title: Time-Resolved In Vivo Measurement of Neuropeptide Dynamics by Capacitive Immunoprobe in Porcine Heart
protocol: Cut a 25 cm length of perfluoroalkoxy (PFA)-coated platinum wire.
Strip approximately 5 mm of PFA coating from one end of the platinum wire using a scalpel.
Insert the stripped end of the platinum wire into a gold-plated 1 mm male connector pin.
Crimp the connector pin teeth around the stripped end of the platinum wire using needle-nose pliers.
Solder the platinum wire to the gold-plated connector pin carefully.
Dissolve 50 mg of dopamine HCl in 50 mL of 10 mM phosphate-buffered saline (PBS, pH 6.0) by stirring.
Place the tip of the platinum wire in the vessel containing the freshly made dopamine-supplemented PBS.
Plug a gold connector pin into a channel of the headstage.
Connect the AgCl disc electrode to the ground channel in the headstage.
Place the AgCl disc in the vessel containing dopamine-supplemented PBS and platinum wire, ensuring only the disc is submerged.
Connect a wire shunt into the reference channels of the headstage.
Open the interactive data acquisition software.
Prepare a sawtooth electrodeposition command potential protocol with start potential = −0.6 V; end potential = +0.65 V; scan rate = 0.04 V∙s-1; duration of deposition = 420 s.
Begin the polydopamine deposition protocol, ensuring all wires are properly connected.
Remove the AgCl ground pellet and the tip of the platinum wire from the vessel after deposition is complete.
Place the tip of the platinum wire into a microtube containing PBS (pH 7.4) for 2-5 min while preparing the antibody solution.
Ensure the wire tip does not contact the sides or bottom of the microtube during placement in the PBS microtube.
Prepare an antibody solution by combining the antibody with PBS (pH 7.4) at a 1:20 ratio.
Soak the polydopamine-deposited tip of the platinum electrode in the antibody solution for a minimum of 2 hours at room temperature.
Rinse the newly-functionalized capacitive immunoprobe (CI probe) tip briefly with PBS (pH 7.4).
Place the functional tip of the CI probe into the flow chamber without disturbing the tip of the electrode.
Pour silicone elastomer into a 35 mm culture dish with an elongated ovoid space-filler in the center of the dish.
Remove the ovoid shape from the hardened elastomer.
Superfuse the chamber with Tris-buffered saline (TBS) and maintain a flow rate of 3 mL/min.
Ensure inflow and outflow keep the fluid level steady to avoid tidal action.
Condition the CI probe with a TBS standard run prior to first experimental test.
Set up command voltage protocol: positive step potential = +100 mV; negative step potential = −5 mV; step duration = 20 ms; acquisition duration = 600 s.
Allow for equilibration of the probe during initial phase of cycling command potential before data acquisition.
Create a solution of the peptide of interest using the same TBS to maintain superfusate composition.
Set up manifold system for switching between TBS and peptide-supplemented TBS without introducing bubbles into tubing or flow chamber.
Set up peptide-sensing data acquisition protocol using TBS standard parameters.
Thread the exposed tip of the platinum wire electrode through a 22 G hypodermic needle, leaving approximately 2 mm beyond the tip of the needle.
Gently bend back the tip of the platinum wire electrode using forceps to create a "barb" that hangs from the end of the hypodermic needle.
Withdraw the needle gently, ensuring enough wire remains for placement in the vessel without the needle contacting the fluid.
Ensure the entire electrical setup is properly grounded before connecting the CI probe to the headstage.
Anesthetize the animals following a previously published report.
Perform surgery to expose the region of interest.
Expose the heart by performing a median sternotomy.
Gently remove the functionalized tip from the PBS rinse.
Attach the hydodermic needle to the barbed C.I. probe.
Implant the probe in the region of interest.
Withdraw the hypodermic needle, leaving the electrode in place.
Proceed with standard testing protocols.
Proceed with experimental testing protocols.
Euthanize the animal under deep anesthesia via induction of ventricular fibrillation.
